concepts.title: Complex Numbers: Definition, Powers of i and Algebra
concepts.definition: A complex number is of the form a plus i b, where a is the real part, b the imaginary part and i is the square root of minus one with successive powers cycling through i, minus one, minus i and one, and complex numbers add and multiply like binomials with i squared replaced by minus one.
concepts.key_idea: The imaginary unit i satisfies i squared equals minus one, and the algebra of complex numbers follows the same laws as real numbers.

concepts.title: Argand Plane Representation of Complex Numbers and Their Absolute Value
concepts.definition: The modulus of a complex number a plus i b is the non-negative square root of a squared plus b squared, giving its distance from the origin, and its conjugate a minus i b reflects it across the real axis, with the product of a number and its conjugate equal to the square of the modulus.
concepts.key_idea: Modulus and conjugate satisfy |z| squared equals z times its conjugate, connecting distance and algebra in the complex plane.
question_patterns: define the modulus of a complex number and compute it
find the conjugate of a given complex number
verify that z times its conjugate equals modulus squared

solution_steps.action: sum the squares and take the square root
solution_steps.explain: Add the squares of the real and imaginary parts and take the square root to get the modulus

concepts.title: Quadratic Equations with Complex Roots
concepts.definition: A quadratic equation ax squared plus bx plus c equals zero with negative discriminant b squared minus four ac has no real roots, and its roots are the pair of complex conjugates given by the quadratic formula with i times the square root of the negative discriminant over two a.
concepts.key_idea: When the discriminant is negative, the quadratic formula still gives the two roots as complex conjugates, completing the solution of every quadratic equation.
